page_title: TypeCue - press a key, it types the line

sources.entry: TypeCue - Types a prepared script into any app, one hotkey press per line, as real keystrokes at a human pace, for demo recordings and live presentations. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/alexpolonsky/TypeCue) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: TypeCue
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS menu bar app that types a prepared script into any app, one hotkey press per line, as real keystrokes at a human pace.
use_cases: film or TV scenes needing real typed text on screen
summary.what_it_does: TypeCue lets you write an ordered list of text blocks ahead of time, one per beat of a demo or scene. Each press of one hotkey (default Ctrl+Option+X) types the next block into whatever app has focus. Typing is sent as system-level key events rather than a clipboard paste, with pacing controlled by inline markers such as [0.5] pauses, [speed:40] tempo changes, and [enter] submits. An always-on-top panel shows what has been typed, what is typing, and what is next. Scripts are stored as a plain JSON file that can be edited by hand or by AI agents, which can also drive the app through typecue:// URL commands.
notable: Sends real keystrokes at a human pace with timing variation at spaces and punctuation, not clipboard paste
Scripts are plain JSON with inline pacing markers; agents like Claude Code or Cursor can author and control it via typecue:// commands
No account, no network calls, no analytics; MIT licensed and installable via Homebrew cask
Layout-aware typing with Unicode fallback and RTL support
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later and Accessibility permission
Cannot type into macOS secure fields (e.g. passwords); those must be entered manually
Built for performing demos rather than everyday text expansion shortcuts
